units.translation: Rhythms. This stasimon is composed in four strophes and antistrophes in the usual manner. The first three strophes are wholly or largely trochaic, while the fourth is iambic, thus in the customary sequence of these genres; see on ⟦1⟧. The first strophes are correspondingly also calmer in ethos; in the last there is more tragic pathos, and certainly also a somewhat quicker tempo. In strophe ⟦2⟧ the trochaic dimeter prevails, in the forms -- c-cr- and ----, once also (which is not frequent) acatalectic – ~~~ -ut; only the fifth (middle) of the nine cola is a trimeter, of the form -rc-clcr. Even simpler is the second strophe in eight cola: colon 4 is a trimeter of the same form, all the others dimeters of the one form - (「. This same form also begins the third strophe, repeated twice; but then there is strong variation; a monometer, which one must probably separate off, and now twice 5 + 2 dactyls, the first time without, the second with internal catalexis in the fifth foot, this exactly as ⟦3⟧: ⟦4⟧. As now in the Persians a brachycatalectic trochaic dimeter is appended, so in the Eumenides the first time a catalectic one, as usual after dactyls (see the first stasimon, strophe ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧); also the second time, if the antistrophe with ⟦7⟧ is to be authoritative; cf. on this below. In any case there then follows as the last colon (from ⟦8⟧, and equal to the last in d) --- Lan. The combination of CICT/IC, -- we also have at ⟦9⟧ as a strophe-ending, but not after trochees; before and after such in the middle of the strophe ⟦10⟧; otherwise - -, - (a form in which one often closes) is found after iambs, as ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧, Cicirilicir, ici, -, since indeed this closing colon consists of a choriambus = diiambus and a catalectic diiambus. Thus rhythmically considered, ⟦13⟧ antistr. (Heath) = ⟦14⟧⟨⟦15⟧⟩ ⟦16⟧ strophe is equally possible. The same colon - then also begins the last strophe; there follow five iambic hexapodies: u-ciri- - - twice, --, then --., I finally - lilcir, and as strophe-ending choriambic-iambic - I,II/II, cii. Content. In the first three strophes (⟦17⟧. ⟦18⟧. ⟦19⟧, ⟦20⟧. ⟦21⟧) the Erinyes express their view of the impending legal decision: if Orestes is not condemned, then all moral reverence, especially toward parents, will be lost among men. But from the second antistrophe onward general moral principles are preached, in exactly the same manner as later by Athena in her foundation speech 690ff.: without a power that inspires fear, no state can exist; the commands of justice must be observed; whoever does so has blessing, but the transgressor perishes, as is set forth in the closing strophes (str. ant. ⟦22⟧) in a powerful and vivid way. The political tendency, then, which the play had alongside everything else, already comes to light here. As the addressee one must think of the people of Athens, who are gathering for the impending legal decision (566).
